exposure: fetal growth restriction in pregnant women with pre-eclampsia
outcome: neonates with Apgar scores <7 at 5 min
abnormal Doppler indices (umbilical artery and mid cerebral artery)
cohort: The study included 189 pregnant women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia who gave birth at the University Hospital of Obstetrics and Gynecology "Queen Geraldine" of Tirana.
finding: Fetal growth restriction in patients with pre-eclampsia significantly predicted worse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, including lower gestational age and birth weight, and higher rates of perinatal deaths, stillbirths, and NICU admissions.
mod_finding: The group with pre-eclampsia associated with fetal growth restriction had a significantly higher rate of cesarean deliveries (65.21% vs. 46.85%) compared to the group without FGR.
